web_context.competitor_activity: AMD holds only ~7% AI accelerator market share (up just 0.8% in Q3 2025) and continues to struggle against NVDA's CUDA ecosystem moat. Intel is gaining traction in AI inference via Xeon CPUs and Gaudi accelerators but remains far behind in training workloads; Intel stock has roughly doubled over the past year ($99.62). The primary competitive threat is custom silicon from hyperscalers — Anthropic is purchasing 1 million Google TPUs for 2026 compute (deal worth 'tens of billions'), and OpenAI, Meta, Microsoft, and Amazon are deploying AMD and Broadcom ASICs. Analysts maintain NVDA's software ecosystem (CUDA) and Blackwell Ultra's performance lead ('two generations ahead') sustain its dominance near-term.
